title: Answer: freedom is partial self-determination, never absolute

statements.text: There is free will in the sense that every occasion is partly self-determining in how it takes its past into account, and the human mind has the most of it on this planet. Agency is mental causation, upward, self-determining and downward. There is no absolute freedom, since every occasion is conditioned by its standpoint.

sources.quote: self-determination gives rise to the probabilistic laws of science as well as human freedom
there is no such fact as absolute freedom; every actual entity possesses only such freedom, as is inherent in the primary phase
